title: Rhythm of Play
text: Core loop of play: GM sets the scene, players declare actions, GM narrates results.

title: The Six Abilities
text: Every creature has six abilities measuring body and mind; see the descriptions table.

title: Ability Descriptions
text: Table: what each ability covers, from Strength (might) to Charisma (poise and charm).

title: Ability Scores
text: Ability scores run 1 to 20 for most, up to 30 for some monsters.

title: Ability Scores
text: Table: score meanings; 10–11 is human average, 20 is the adventurer cap, 30 the absolute max.

title: Ability Modifiers
text: Each score yields a modifier added to D20 Tests; always round fractions down unless told otherwise.

title: Ability Modifiers
text: Table: score-to-modifier conversion, from −5 at score 1 to +10 at score 30.

title: D20 Tests
text: Uncertain actions use a d20 roll plus modifiers versus a target: checks, saves, or attack rolls.

title: Ability Checks
text: Ability checks resolve non-attack tasks with real risk of failure, like forcing doors or picking locks.

title: Ability Modifier
text: A check takes its name from the ability modifier added, e.g. a Wisdom check.

title: Ability Check Examples
text: Table: typical uses for each ability's checks, e.g. Strength to lift or break, Wisdom to notice.

title: Proficiency Bonus
text: When a relevant skill or tool proficiency applies, your Proficiency Bonus goes on the check.

title: Difficulty Class
text: The GM sets each check's DC; harder tasks get a higher number to beat.

title: Typical Difficulty Classes
text: Table: DC 5 very easy, 10 easy, 15 medium, 20 hard, 25 very hard, 30 nearly impossible.

title: Saving Throws
text: Saves resist threats like explosions, poison, or mind spells; you may choose to fail one deliberately.

title: Ability Modifier
text: Each save is labeled by the ability modifier it adds, e.g. a Constitution save.

title: Saving Throw Examples
text: Table: what each ability's save resists, e.g. Dexterity to dodge harm, Wisdom against mental assault.

title: Proficiency Bonus
text: Proficient in a type of save? Your Proficiency Bonus goes on those saves.

title: Difficulty Class
text: Save DCs come from the effect or GM; a spell's DC uses caster ability and Proficiency Bonus.

title: Attack Rolls
text: An attack hits when the roll meets or beats the target's Armor Class.

title: Ability Modifier
text: Table holds which ability modifier each attack type uses.

title: Attack Roll Abilities
text: Table: melee and Unarmed Strikes use Strength, ranged weapons Dexterity, spells your casting ability; Finesse allows either.

title: Proficiency Bonus
text: Add Proficiency Bonus to attacks with proficient weapons and to all spell attacks.

title: Armor Class
text: Base AC is 10 plus Dexterity modifier, then adjusted; only one base AC formula can apply.

title: Rolling 20 or 1
text: A natural 20 on an attack always hits as a Critical Hit; a natural 1 always misses.

title: Advantage/Disadvantage
text: Advantage or Disadvantage changes a D20 Test; Heroic Inspiration lets you reroll one die, holding one at most.

title: Roll Two D20s
text: With Advantage take the higher of two d20s; with Disadvantage take the lower.

title: They Don’t Stack
text: Multiple sources still mean two d20s; having both Advantage and Disadvantage cancels them out entirely.

title: Interactions with Rerolls
text: When rolling two d20s, a reroll or replacement effect applies to just one die of your choice.

title: Proficiency
text: Every creature has a Proficiency Bonus from level or CR, added to proficient skills, saves, and attacks.

title: Proficiency Bonus
text: Table: Proficiency Bonus by level or CR, from +2 at levels 1–4 up to +9 at CR 29–30.

title: The Bonus Doesn’t Stack
text: Proficiency Bonus is added only once per roll; it can be doubled or halved at most once each.

title: Skill Proficiencies
text: Skills are categories of checks; proficiency adds your bonus, and the GM rules which skill applies.

title: Skills
text: Table: all 18 skills, their usual ability, and example uses.

title: Skill List
text: Pointer to the Skills table listing each skill's typical ability and uses.

title: Determining Skills
text: Characters get skill proficiencies at creation; monsters list theirs in the stat block.

title: Saving Throw Proficiencies
text: Save proficiency adds your bonus to that ability's saves; every class grants at least two.

title: Equipment Proficiencies
text: Class and background grant weapon and tool proficiencies; tool plus matching skill proficiency gives Advantage.

title: Actions
text: Anything besides moving or talking usually costs an action; see the actions table.

title: Actions
text: Table: the main actions (Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Hide, Influence, and more) with brief effects.

title: One Thing at a Time
text: Only a single action can be taken at once; this matters most in combat, sometimes elsewhere.

title: Bonus Actions
text: Bonus Actions are extra actions usable only when a feature or spell grants them; one per turn.

title: Reactions
text: Reactions fire immediately when triggered, on your turn or others'; Opportunity Attacks are the classic example.

title: Social Interaction
text: Talking scenes with NPCs; the GM voices them and sets their attitude toward you.

title: Roleplaying
text: Play your character's words and choices, either acting them out or describing them.

title: Ability Checks
text: The GM may call for an Influence check to see how an NPC responds to your approach.

title: Exploration
text: Intro to exploring dangerous places and interacting with the environment.

title: Adventuring Equipment
text: Gear like Ladders, Torches, Thieves' Tools, and Caltrops solves exploration problems.

title: Vision and Light
text: Sight affects noticing danger, attacking, and targeting spells; obscured vision hampers you.

title: Obscured Areas
text: Light obscurement gives Disadvantage on sight-based Perception; heavy obscurement makes you effectively Blinded.

title: Light
text: Three light levels: Bright (normal sight), Dim (lightly obscured), Darkness (heavily obscured).

title: Special Senses
text: Special senses defined in the glossary: Blindsight, Darkvision, Tremorsense, and Truesight.

title: Hiding
text: The GM judges when hiding is possible; attempting it uses the Hide action.

title: Interacting with Objects
text: Most object use is simply described and narrated; some rules govern special cases.

title: What Is an Object?
text: Objects are single inanimate items like doors or swords, not buildings or vehicles.

title: Time-Limited Object Interactions
text: In combat you get one free object interaction per turn; extra ones need the Utilize action.

title: Finding Hidden Objects
text: Searching for hidden things calls for Wisdom (Perception), but only if you look in the right area.

title: Carrying Objects
text: Weight usually doesn't matter; the GM may apply carrying capacity rules for very heavy loads.

title: Breaking Objects
text: Break fragile nonmagical objects automatically with an action; tougher things use glossary rules; also covers marching order.

title: Hazards
text: Non-monster dangers in the glossary: burning, falling, suffocation, dehydration, and malnutrition.

title: Travel
text: Long trips can be summarized by the GM or tracked with travel pace rules.

title: Travel Pace
text: Pick a Slow, Normal, or Fast travel pace; mounts can double distance for 1 hour.

title: Travel Pace
text: Table: pace per minute/hour/day (Fast 30 miles, Normal 24, Slow 18) and each pace's check effects.

title: Vehicles
text: Land vehicles use normal paces; ships move at vessel speed and may sail up to 24 hours daily.

title: Combat
text: Intro to the combat rules for fights with monsters and villains.

title: The Order of Combat
text: Combat runs in rounds of about 6 seconds, each participant taking one turn.

title: Combat Step by Step
text: Combat steps: GM sets positions, everyone rolls Initiative, then turns proceed round by round.

title: Initiative
text: Initiative is a Dexterity check setting turn order; surprised combatants roll it at Disadvantage.

title: Your Turn
text: Each turn: move as far as your Speed allows plus one action, any order; brief talk is free.

title: Ending Combat
text: Combat ends when a side is killed, knocked out, surrenders, flees, or both agree to stop.

title: Movement and Position
text: Spend your Speed on walking, climbing, swimming, crawling, or jumping, mixed as you like.

title: Difficult Terrain
text: Each foot moved through Difficult Terrain costs 2 feet, no matter how many hindrances overlap.

title: Breaking Up Your Move
text: Split your movement around actions, Bonus Actions, and Reactions within the same turn.

title: Dropping Prone
text: Go Prone on your turn for free, using no action or movement, unless your Speed is 0.

title: Creature Size
text: Size category sets how much map space a creature occupies; sizes run Tiny to Gargantuan.

title: Creature Size and Space
text: Table: space per size, from Tiny (2½ ft) to Gargantuan (20 ft, 4 by 4 squares).

title: Moving around Other Creatures
text: You can pass through allies, Incapacitated, Tiny, or two-sizes-different creatures; ending in an occupied space makes you Prone.

title: Making an Attack
text: How to make an attack; unseen targets give you Disadvantage, unseen attackers get Advantage.

title: Cover
text: Cover grants a target bonuses to AC and Dexterity saves, in three degrees.

title: Cover
text: Table: Half cover +2 AC and Dex saves, Three-Quarters +5, Total means no direct targeting.

title: Ranged Attacks
text: Ranged attacks hit foes at distance with bows, thrown weapons, or spells.

title: Range
text: Attacks past normal range have Disadvantage; you can't attack beyond long range.

title: Ranged Attacks in Close Combat
text: Ranged attack rolls have Disadvantage if an enemy within 5 feet can see you and isn't Incapacitated.

title: Melee Attacks
text: Melee attacks target creatures within reach using weapons, Unarmed Strikes, or natural weapons.

title: Reach
text: Standard reach is 5 feet; some creatures reach farther.

title: Opportunity Attacks
text: Leaving an enemy's reach provokes a Reaction attack; Disengage or Teleport avoids it.

title: Mounted Combat
text: Any willing creature one or more sizes bigger than you, and suitably built, can be ridden.

title: Mounting and Dismounting
text: Mounting or dismounting a creature within 5 feet costs half your Speed.

title: Controlling a Mount
text: Trained mounts share your Initiative and can only Dash, Disengage, or Dodge; independent mounts act freely.

title: Falling Off
text: Mount forcibly moved or knocked Prone: make a DC 10 Dex save or fall off Prone.

title: Underwater Combat
text: Special rules apply to fighting underwater.

title: Impeded Weapons
text: Underwater melee without Swim Speed has Disadvantage unless Piercing; ranged attacks miss past normal range.

title: Fire Resistance
text: While submerged, every creature and object resists Fire damage.

title: Damage and Healing
text: Rules for injury, healing, and death.

title: Hit Points
text: Hit Points measure toughness; damage lowers them toward 0; rests restore them.

title: Damage Rolls
text: Roll the listed damage dice plus modifiers; weapon damage adds the attack's ability modifier; minimum 0.

title: Critical Hits
text: On a Critical Hit, roll all damage dice twice, including extras like Sneak Attack, then add modifiers.

title: Saving Throws and Damage
text: Rules for damage dealt through saving throws.

title: Damage against Multiple Targets
text: Roll damage once for an area effect and apply it to every target that saves.

title: Half Damage
text: A successful save often means half damage, rounded down.

title: Damage Types
text: Every damage instance has a type, such as Fire or Slashing, which other rules reference.

title: Resistance and Vulnerability
text: Resistance halves damage of that type (round down); Vulnerability doubles it.

title: No Stacking
text: Overlapping Resistances or Vulnerabilities to one damage type count only once.

title: Order of Application
text: Damage order: apply bonuses, penalties, and multipliers first, then Resistance, then Vulnerability.

title: Immunity
text: Immunity means no damage of that type, or no effect from that condition.

title: Healing
text: Magic and rests restore HP, capped at your max; melee kills can become knockouts instead.

title: Dropping to 0 Hit Points
text: At 0 Hit Points a creature either dies or falls unconscious.

title: Instant Death
text: Monsters die at 0 HP; anyone dies at 0 max HP or when leftover damage equals their max.

title: Character Demise
text: A dead character may be revived by magic like Raise Dead, or replaced with a new one.

title: Falling Unconscious
text: At 0 HP without dying you're Unconscious and start making Death Saving Throws.

title: Death Saving Throws
text: Start a turn at 0 HP: roll d20, 10+ succeeds; three successes stabilize, three failures kill.

title: Stabilizing a Character
text: Help plus a DC 10 Medicine check stabilizes a dying ally; 1 HP returns after 1d4 hours.

title: Temporary Hit Points
text: Temporary Hit Points act as a buffer absorbed before your real HP.

title: Lose Temporary Hit Points First
text: Damage strips Temporary Hit Points first, then any excess comes off your HP.

title: Duration
text: Temp HP stay until they're spent or a Long Rest ends.

title: They Don’t Stack
text: Temporary HP never add together; when gaining more, keep whichever amount you prefer.

title: They’re Not Hit Points or Healing
text: Temp HP aren't healing, can't be healed, and won't wake you from 0 HP.

title: Choose a Character Sheet
text: Keep your adventurer’s details on whatever sheet or format suits you.

title: Create Your Character
text: Five creation steps: choose class, determine origin, set ability scores, pick alignment, fill in details.

title: Step 1: Choose Class
text: Pick a class and note it; the overview table summarizes each option.

title: Class Overview
text: Table: each class's theme, primary ability, and complexity rating.

title: Write Your Level
text: Record your level and XP; start at level 1 with 0 XP unless the GM says otherwise.

title: Note Armor Training
text: Note which armor categories your class trains you in, so you gain their AC benefits.

title: Step 2: Character Origin
text: Your origin is your chosen background and species plus two languages.

title: Choose a Background
text: Pick a background; it shapes your ability score increases, feat, and proficiencies.

title: Ability Scores and Backgrounds
text: Table of background ability options; backgrounds also grant a feat, two skills, and one tool proficiency.

title: Choose Starting Equipment
text: Class and background both give starting gear; spend any coins on equipment now.

title: Choose a Species
text: Choose one of nine species, such as Elf, Dwarf, Orc, or Tiefling, and record its traits.

title: Imagine Your Past and Present
text: Prompts for inventing your character's history, such as who raised you and childhood friends.

title: Choose Languages
text: Start knowing Common and two more standard languages, rolled or picked from the table.

title: Standard Languages
text: Table: d12 roll for standard languages like Draconic, Dwarvish, Elvish, and Orc.

title: Rare Languages
text: Table: rare languages like Abyssal, Celestial, Infernal, and Primordial with its four dialects.

title: Step 3: Ability Scores
text: Create six numbers, then place one in each ability.

title: Generate Your Scores
text: Three methods: 27-point buy, roll 4d6 keeping the top three, or the standard array (15 down to 8).

title: Ability Score Point Costs
text: Table: point-buy costs, from 0 points for an 8 up to 9 points for a 15.

title: Assign Ability Scores
text: Assign your six scores with your class's primary ability in mind, then note modifiers.

title: Standard Array by Class
text: Table: suggested standard array placement for each class.

title: Adjust Ability Scores
text: Raise background-listed abilities by +2 and +1, or +1 to all three; max 20.

title: Determine Ability Modifiers
text: Look up each score's modifier on the table and record it.

title: Ability Scores and Modifiers
text: Table: score-to-modifier conversion for scores 3 through 20.

title: Step 4: Alignment
text: Pick an alignment; evil characters need GM approval.

title: The Nine Alignments
text: Alignment combines morality (good, neutral, evil) with attitude to order (lawful, neutral, chaotic).

title: Step 5: Character Creation Details
text: Finish the remaining entries on the character sheet.

title: Record Class Features
text: Write down your level 1 class features and make any choices they offer.

title: Fill In Numbers
text: Record save, skill, Passive Perception, HP, Hit Dice, Initiative, AC, and attack totals.

title: Level 1 Hit Points by Class
text: Table: level 1 HP by class: Barbarian 12, Fighter/Paladin/Ranger 10, most 8, Sorcerer/Wizard 6, plus Con.

title: Level Advancement
text: Gain XP by adventuring; reaching set totals raises your level.

title: Character Advancement
text: Table: XP needed and Proficiency Bonus for levels 1–20 (300 XP for level 2, 355,000 for 20).

title: Gaining a Level
text: Leveling up: pick a class, add a Hit Die and roll or take fixed HP, record new features.

title: Fixed Hit Points by Class
text: Table: fixed HP per level, from Barbarian 7 + Con down to Sorcerer/Wizard 4 + Con.

title: Tiers of Play
text: Campaigns span four tiers by level, each raising the stakes and power.

title: Tier 1 (Levels 1–4)
text: Levels 1–4: apprentice heroes pick subclasses and face local threats.

title: Tier 2 (Levels 5–10)
text: Levels 5–10: big spells like Fireball and multiple attacks; threats to cities and kingdoms.

title: Tier 3 (Levels 11–16)
text: Levels 11–16: reality-bending spells and more attacks; heroes stand out among adventurers.

title: Tier 4 (Levels 17–20)
text: Levels 17–20: peak class features; the world or multiverse may hang in the balance.

title: Starting at Higher Levels
text: The GM may start characters above level 1; level 3 suits experienced players.

title: Creating Your Character
text: Build higher-level characters using normal creation steps plus the leveling rules.

title: Starting Equipment at Higher Levels
text: Table: extra starting gold and magic items by starting level; plus optional post-20 feats.

title: Starting Equipment
text: The GM decides extra starting gear or magic items for higher-level characters.

title: Multiclassing
text: On leveling, you may pick up a different class instead of advancing your current one.

title: Prerequisites
text: To multiclass, both your current and new classes' primary abilities must be 13 or higher.

title: Experience Points
text: Level-up XP thresholds follow your combined level across all classes.

title: Hit Points and Hit Point Dice
text: Gain later-level HP for a new class; same-size Hit Dice pool together, different sizes tracked separately.

title: Proficiency Bonus
text: Proficiency Bonus depends on total character level, not individual class levels.

title: Proficiencies
text: A new multiclass grants only part of its starting proficiencies, as listed per class.

title: Class Features
text: You gain each class's features by its level; Extra Attack, Spellcasting, and AC have special rules.

title: Armor Class
text: With multiple AC formulas from different classes, choose just one to use.

title: Extra Attack
text: Extra Attack from multiple classes doesn't stack beyond two attacks unless a feature says otherwise.

title: Spellcasting
text: Prepare spells per class separately, but combine caster levels to find spell slots.

title: Multiclass Spellcaster: Spell Slots per Spell Level
text: Table: slots available at each spell level for multiclass casters, by combined level 1–20.

title: Trinkets
text: Optionally roll once for a free Tiny trinket, a small curious item.

title: Trinkets
text: Table: d100 list of 100 odd trinkets to roll for.

title: Barbarian
text: Barbarian: Strength-based melee class driven by Rage.

title: Core Barbarian Traits
text: Barbarian: Str primary, d12 Hit Die, Str/Con saves, martial weapons, light/medium armor and shields.

title: Becoming a Barbarian …
text: How to start as a Barbarian at level 1 or via multiclass.

title: As a Level 1 Character
text: At level 1 as a Barbarian, take every core trait in the table.

title: Barbarian Features
text: Table: Barbarian Proficiency Bonus and features by level, 1–20.

title: As a Multiclass Character
text: Barbarian multiclass gets the Hit Die, Martial weapons, Shields, and level 1 features.

title: Barbarian Class Features
text: Barbarian features gained at specific levels, per the Barbarian Features table.

title: Level 1: Rage
text: Bonus Action: Rage for bonus damage and physical-damage resistance; 2 uses at level 1, no Heavy armor.

title: Level 1: Unarmored Defense
text: With no armor, AC equals 10 + Dex + Con modifiers; a Shield still works.

title: Level 1: Weapon Mastery
text: Unlock mastery effects for two melee weapon kinds; swap one per Long Rest; more later.

title: Level 2: Danger Sense
text: Advantage on Dexterity saves unless you're Incapacitated.

title: Level 2: Reckless Attack
text: Gain Advantage on Strength attacks this turn, but enemies get Advantage against you until your next turn.

title: Level 3: Barbarian Subclass
text: Choose a Barbarian subclass such as Path of the Berserker; get its features at listed levels.

title: Level 3: Primal Knowledge
text: Gain one extra Barbarian skill; while raging, some Dex/Wis/Cha skill checks can use Strength.

title: Level 4: Ability Score Improvement
text: Gain Ability Score Improvement or another feat; repeats at levels 16, 12, and 8.

title: Level 5: Extra Attack
text: Taking the Attack action now gives you two attacks.

title: Level 5: Fast Movement
text: Gain +10 feet of Speed when not in Heavy armor.

title: Level 7: Feral Instinct
text: Advantage on Initiative rolls.

title: Level 7: Instinctive Pounce
text: Entering Rage also lets you move half your Speed as part of it.

title: Level 9: Brutal Strike
text: Trade Reckless Attack's Advantage on one hit for +1d10 damage and a push or slow effect.

title: Level 11: Relentless Rage
text: At 0 HP while raging, DC 10 Con save keeps you up at 2 × Barbarian level HP.

title: Level 13: Improved Brutal Strike
text: Adds Staggering Blow (target's next save has Disadvantage) and Sundering Blow (next ally attack +5).

title: Level 15: Persistent Rage
text: Regain all Rage uses on Initiative once per Long Rest; Rage lasts 10 minutes automatically.

title: Level 17: Improved Brutal Strike
text: Brutal Strike damage rises to 2d10, and you may apply two different effects.

title: Level 18: Indomitable Might
text: A Strength check or save never totals below your Strength score.

title: Level 19: Epic Boon
text: Gain an Epic Boon or other feat; Irresistible Offense is the suggested pick.

title: Level 20: Primal Champion
text: Add 4 to both Strength and Constitution, which can now reach 25.

title: Barbarian Subclass: Path of the Berserker
text: Berserker subclass: channels Rage into raw offensive violence.

title: Level 3: Frenzy
text: Raging and reckless, your first hit each turn adds a d6 per point of Rage Damage bonus.

title: Level 6: Mindless Rage
text: While raging, immune to Charmed and Frightened; entering Rage ends those conditions.

title: Level 10: Retaliation
text: Reaction: strike back with a melee attack at a creature within 5 feet that damages you.

title: Level 14: Intimidating Presence
text: Bonus Action: chosen foes within 30 ft save (Wis) or are Frightened 1 minute; 1/Long Rest.

title: Bard
text: Bard: Charisma-based spellcaster and skill expert who inspires allies.

title: Core Bard Traits
text: Bard: Cha primary, d8 Hit Die, Dex/Cha saves, any 3 skills, 3 instruments, light armor.

title: Becoming a Bard …
text: How to start as a Bard at level 1 or via multiclass.

title: As a Level 1 Character
text: At level 1 as a Bard, take every core trait in the table.

title: Bard Features
text: Table: Bard features, Proficiency Bonus, and Bardic Inspiration die (d6 to d12) by level.

title: As a Multiclass Character
text: Bard multiclass gets the Hit Die, one skill, one instrument, Light armor, and level 1 features.

title: Bard Class Features
text: Bard features gained at specific levels, per the Bard Features table.

title: Level 1: Bardic Inspiration
text: Bonus Action: grant an ally within 60 ft a d6 to boost a failed d20 roll; Cha-mod uses.

title: Level 1: Spellcasting
text: Cast Bard spells using Charisma; 2 cantrips and 4 prepared spells at level 1.

title: Level 2: Expertise
text: Expertise in two proficient skills, doubling the bonus; two more at level 9.

title: Level 2: Jack of All Trades
text: Checks with skills you aren't proficient in get half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down.

title: Level 3: Bard Subclass
text: Choose a Bard subclass such as College of Lore; get its features at listed levels.

title: Level 4: Ability Score Improvement
text: Gain Ability Score Improvement or another feat; repeats at levels 16, 12, and 8.

title: Level 5: Font of Inspiration
text: Bardic Inspiration recharges on Short or Long Rests; spend a spell slot to regain one use.

title: Level 7: Countercharm
text: Reaction: when you or someone within 30 ft fails a save against Charmed or Frightened, reroll with Advantage.

title: Level 10: Magical Secrets
text: When your prepared spell count rises, new picks can come from Cleric, Druid, or Wizard lists.

title: Level 18: Superior Inspiration
text: On rolling Initiative, regain Bardic Inspiration up to at least two uses.

title: Level 19: Epic Boon
text: Gain an Epic Boon or other feat; Spell Recall is the suggested pick.

title: Level 20: Words of Creation
text: Always have Power Word Heal and Kill prepared; each can hit a second target within 10 feet.

title: Bard Spell List
text: Bard spells by level and school, marked for Concentration, Ritual, or Material components.

title: Bard Subclass: College of Lore
text: College of Lore subclass: gathers knowledge and spells from many traditions.

title: Level 3: Bonus Proficiencies
text: Become proficient in any three skills you choose.

title: Level 3: Cutting Words
text: Reaction: spend Inspiration to reduce a creature's damage, check, or attack roll within 60 ft.

title: Level 6: Magical Discoveries
text: Learn two always-prepared spells taken from Wizard, Druid, or Cleric lists.

title: Level 14: Peerless Skill
text: After failing a check or attack, add Bardic Inspiration; it isn't spent if you still fail.

title: Cleric
text: Cleric: Wisdom-based divine caster, healer, and support class.

title: Core Cleric Traits
text: Cleric: Wis primary, d8 Hit Die, Wis/Cha saves, simple weapons, light/medium armor and shields.

title: Becoming a Cleric …
text: How to start as a Cleric at level 1 or via multiclass.

title: As a Level 1 Character
text: At level 1 as a Cleric, take all core traits and level 1 features.

title: Cleric Features
text: Table: Cleric features, Proficiency Bonus, and Channel Divinity uses by level.

title: As a Multiclass Character
text: Cleric multiclass gets the Hit Die, Light/Medium armor and Shields, and level 1 features.

title: Cleric Class Features
text: Cleric features gained at specific levels, per the Cleric Features table.

title: Level 1: Spellcasting
text: Cast Cleric spells using Wisdom; 3 cantrips and 4 prepared spells at level 1.

title: Level 1: Divine Order
text: Pick Protector (martial weapons, Heavy armor) or Thaumaturge (extra cantrip, Wis bonus to Arcana/Religion).

title: Level 2: Channel Divinity
text: Use Divine Spark or Turn Undead; 2 uses, one back on Short Rest, all on Long Rest.

title: Level 3: Cleric Subclass
text: Choose a Cleric subclass such as Life Domain; get its features at listed levels.

title: Level 4: Ability Score Improvement
text: Gain Ability Score Improvement or another feat; repeats at levels 16, 12, and 8.

title: Level 5: Sear Undead
text: Turn Undead also deals Radiant damage of Wis-mod d8s to Undead that fail their save.

title: Level 7: Blessed Strikes
text: Choose Divine Strike (+1d8 Necrotic/Radiant weapon damage once per turn) or Potent Spellcasting (+Wis to cantrips).

title: Level 10: Divine Intervention
text: Magic action: cast any Cleric spell up to 5th level with no slot; once per Long Rest.

title: Level 14: Improved Blessed Strikes
text: Divine Strike grows to 2d8; Potent Spellcasting cantrips also grant temp HP equal to twice Wis.

title: Level 19: Epic Boon
text: Take an Epic Boon or other feat; Boon of Fate is suggested.

title: Level 20: Greater Divine Intervention
text: Divine Intervention can cast Wish, but then it's unusable for 2d4 Long Rests.

title: Cleric Spell List
text: Cleric spells by level and school, marked for Concentration, Ritual, or Material components.

title: Cleric Subclass: Life Domain
text: Life Domain subclass: a healing specialist drawing on positive energy.

title: Level 3: Disciple of Life
text: Slot-cast healing spells restore an extra 2 + slot level HP.

title: Level 3: Life Domain Spells
text: Always have Life Domain spells prepared at the listed Cleric levels.

title: Life Domain Spells
text: Table: Life Domain spells: Aid, Bless, Cure Wounds at 3 up to Mass Cure Wounds at 9.

title: Level 3: Preserve Life
text: Channel Divinity: split 5 × Cleric level HP among Bloodied creatures within 30 ft, up to half max.

title: Level 6: Blessed Healer
text: Casting slot healing on others also heals you for 2 + slot level.

title: Level 17: Supreme Healing
text: Healing dice from spells or Channel Divinity always give their maximum result.

title: Druid
text: Druid: Wisdom-based nature caster who can shape-shift into beasts.

title: Core Druid Traits
text: Druid: Wis primary, d8 Hit Die, Int/Wis saves, Herbalism Kit, light armor and shields.

title: Druid Features
text: Table: Druid features, Proficiency Bonus, and Wild Shape uses by level.

title: Becoming a Druid …
text: How to start as a Druid at level 1 or via multiclass.

title: As a Level 1 Character
text: At level 1 as a Druid, take all core traits and level 1 features.

title: As a Multiclass Character
text: Druid multiclass gets the Hit Die, Light armor and Shields, and level 1 features.

title: Druid Class Features
text: Druid features gained at specific levels, per the Druid Features table.

title: Level 1: Spellcasting
text: Cast Druid spells using Wisdom; spell slot and prepared spell table included.

title: Level 1: Druidic
text: Know the secret Druidic language and always have Speak with Animals prepared.

title: Level 1: Primal Order
text: Pick Magician (extra cantrip, Wis bonus to Arcana/Nature) or Warden (martial weapons, Medium armor).

title: Level 2: Wild Shape
text: Bonus Action: turn into a known Beast for half Druid level hours; 2 uses per rest cycle.

title: Beast Shapes
text: Table: forms known, max CR, and flying by level; transforming gives temp HP equal to Druid level.

title: Level 2: Wild Companion
text: Spend a spell slot or Wild Shape to cast Find Familiar as a Fey spirit, no material cost.

title: Level 3: Druid Subclass
text: Choose a Druid subclass such as Circle of the Land; get its features at listed levels.

title: Level 4: Ability Score Improvement
text: Gain Ability Score Improvement or another feat; repeats at levels 16, 12, and 8.

title: Level 5: Wild Resurgence
text: Spend a slot to refill an empty Wild Shape, or vice versa for a level 1 slot.

title: Level 7: Elemental Fury
text: Choose Potent Spellcasting (+Wis to cantrip damage) or Primal Strike (+1d8 elemental damage once per turn).

title: Level 15: Improved Elemental Fury
text: Potent Spellcasting gives cantrips +300 ft range; Primal Strike grows to 2d8.

title: Level 18: Beast Spells
text: Cast spells while in Wild Shape, except costly or consumed material components.

title: Level 19: Epic Boon
text: Take an Epic Boon or other feat; Boon of Dimensional Travel is suggested.

title: Level 20: Archdruid
text: Regain Wild Shape on Initiative, convert Wild Shape uses into spell slots, and age slowly.

title: Druid Spell List
text: Druid spells by level and school, marked for Concentration, Ritual, or Material components.

title: Druid Subclass: Circle of the Land
text: Circle of the Land subclass: druids drawing magic from particular landscapes.

title: Level 3: Circle of the Land Spells
text: Each Long Rest, choose a land type (arid, tropical, polar, temperate) for its prepared spells.

title: Arid Land
text: Table: arid spells, e.g. Burning Hands at 3, Fireball at 5, Wall of Stone at 9.

title: Polar Land
text: Table: polar spells, e.g. Ray of Frost at 3, Ice Storm at 7, Cone of Cold at 9.

title: Temperate Land
text: Table: temperate spells, including Misty Step and Sleep at 3, up to Tree Stride at 9.

title: Tropical Land
text: Table: tropical spells, including Web and Acid Splash at 3, up to Insect Plague at 9.

title: Level 3: Land’s Aid
text: Spend Wild Shape: 10-ft sphere deals 2d6 Necrotic (Con save halves) and heals one creature 2d6.

title: Level 6: Natural Recovery
text: Cast one circle spell free per Long Rest; recover slots totaling half Druid level on a Short Rest.

title: Level 10: Nature’s Ward
text: Immune to Poisoned and resistant to your chosen land's damage type.

title: Nature’s Ward
text: Table: land resistances: arid Fire, polar Cold, temperate Lightning, tropical Poison.

title: Level 14: Nature’s Sanctuary
text: Spend Wild Shape: a 15-ft cube grants allies Half Cover and your Nature's Ward resistance for 1 minute.

title: Fighter
text: Fighter: versatile weapons expert with the most attacks and martial options.

title: Core Fighter Traits
text: Fighter: Str or Dex primary, d10 Hit Die, Str/Con saves, all weapons, all armor and shields.

title: Fighter Features
text: Table: Fighter features, Proficiency Bonus, Second Wind uses, and mastery count by level.

title: Becoming a Fighter …
text: How to start as a Fighter at level 1 or via multiclass.

title: As a Level 1 Character
text: At level 1 as a Fighter, take all core traits and level 1 features.

title: As a Multiclass Character
text: Fighter multiclass gets the Hit Die, Martial weapons, Light/Medium armor and Shields, and level 1 features.

title: Fighter Class Features
text: Fighter features gained at specific levels, per the Fighter Features table.

title: Level 1: Fighting Style
text: Pick a Fighting Style feat (Defense suggested); may change it on each level-up.

title: Level 1: Second Wind
text: Bonus Action: heal 1d10 + Fighter level; 2 uses, one back on Short Rest, all on Long Rest.

title: Level 1: Weapon Mastery
text: Use mastery properties of three weapon types; swap one per Long Rest; more at higher levels.

title: Level 2: Action Surge
text: Take one extra non-Magic action on your turn; once per rest, twice from level 17.

title: Level 2: Tactical Mind
text: On a failed check, spend Second Wind to add 1d10; not spent if it still fails.

title: Level 3: Fighter Subclass
text: Pick your Fighter specialization at level 3; it grants extra features as you level (Champion included).

title: Level 4: Ability Score Improvement
text: Gain an ASI feat or any feat you qualify for; again at 6, 8, 12, 14, 16.

title: Level 5: Extra Attack
text: Attack action now lets you make two attacks.

title: Level 5: Tactical Shift
text: Using Second Wind also lets you move up to half Speed, free of Opportunity Attacks.

title: Level 9: Indomitable
text: Reroll a failed save plus your Fighter level; once per Long Rest (twice at 13, thrice at 17).

title: Level 9: Tactical Master
text: Swap a weapon's mastery property for Push, Sap, or Slow on any attack.

title: Level 11: Two Extra Attacks
text: Attack action now lets you make three attacks.

title: Level 13: Studied Attacks
text: Miss a creature and you get Advantage against it on the following attack, until your next turn ends.

title: Level 19: Epic Boon
text: Gain an Epic Boon or other qualifying feat; Boon of Combat Prowess suggested.

title: Level 20: Three Extra Attacks
text: Attack action now lets you make four attacks.

title: Fighter Subclass: Champion
text: Fighter subclass built on raw martial skill: wider crit range, athletics, and staying power.

title: Level 3: Improved Critical
text: Weapon and Unarmed Strike attacks crit on a natural 19 or 20.

title: Level 3: Remarkable Athlete
text: Advantage on Initiative and Strength (Athletics); after a crit, move half Speed without Opportunity Attacks.

title: Level 7: Additional Fighting Style
text: Choose one more Fighting Style feat.

title: Level 10: Heroic Warrior
text: In combat, gain Heroic Inspiration at the start of any turn you lack it.

title: Level 15: Superior Critical
text: Weapon and Unarmed Strike attacks now crit on 18 to 20.

title: Level 18: Survivor
text: Advantage on Death Saves (18+ counts as a 20); while Bloodied, heal 5 + Con mod each turn.

title: Monk
text: Class heading: the Monk, a Dex/Wis unarmed warrior fueled by Focus Points.

title: Core Monk Traits
text: Monk basics: Dex and Wis primary, d8 Hit Die, Str and Dex saves, 2 skills, no armor.

title: Becoming a Monk …
text: Section on how to take the Monk class, new or multiclassing.

title: As a Level 1 Character
text: Starting as a Monk: take every core trait plus the level 1 Monk features.

title: As a Multiclass Character
text: Multiclassing into Monk: gain only its Hit Die plus level 1 Monk features.

title: Monk Class Features
text: Intro: Monk features unlock by class level; see the class table.

title: Monk Features
text: Table: proficiency bonus, features, Martial Arts die, Focus Points and movement bonus by level 1 to 20.

title: Level 1: Martial Arts
text: Unarmored with Monk weapons: Bonus Action Unarmed Strike, d6 Martial Arts die, Dex for attacks.

title: Level 1: Unarmored Defense
text: Without armor or Shield, your AC equals 10 + Dex mod + Wis mod.

title: Level 2: Monk’s Focus
text: Gain Focus Points per level to fuel Flurry of Blows, Step of the Wind, and Patient Defense.

title: Level 2: Unarmored Movement
text: Speed rises by 10 feet while unarmored and shieldless, growing at higher Monk levels.

title: Level 2: Uncanny Metabolism
text: On Initiative, refill all Focus Points and heal Martial Arts die + Monk level; 1 per Long Rest.

title: Level 3: Deflect Attacks
text: Reaction: cut slashing, piercing or bludgeoning damage by 1d10 + Dex + Monk level; redirect for 1 Focus.

title: Level 3: Monk Subclass
text: Pick your Monk specialization at level 3, such as the Open Hand warrior.

title: Level 4: Ability Score Improvement
text: Gain an ASI feat (raise ability scores) or another feat you qualify for; repeats at 8, 12, 16.

title: Level 4: Slow Fall
text: Reaction when falling: reduce fall damage by 5 times your Monk level.

title: Level 5: Extra Attack
text: Attack action now lets you make two attacks.

title: Level 5: Stunning Strike
text: Once per turn on a hit, spend 1 Focus: Con save or Stunned; on a success, slowed instead.

title: Level 6: Empowered Strikes
text: Your Unarmed Strikes may deal Force damage instead of their usual type.

title: Level 7: Evasion
text: Dex saves for half damage: take none on a success, half on a failure.

title: Level 9: Acrobatic Movement
text: While unarmored, run up walls and across liquids during your turn.

title: Level 10: Heightened Focus
text: Flurry makes 3 strikes, Patient Defense grants temp HP, Step of the Wind carries an ally.

title: Level 10: Self-Restoration
text: End of each turn, shed Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned; no Exhaustion from going without food or water.

title: Level 13: Deflect Energy
text: Deflect Attacks now works against every damage type.

title: Level 14: Disciplined Survivor
text: Proficient in all saves; spend 1 Focus to reroll a failed save.

title: Level 15: Perfect Focus
text: On Initiative without Uncanny Metabolism, top Focus Points back up to 4.

title: Level 18: Superior Defense
text: Spend 3 Focus at turn start: Resistance to all non-Force damage for 1 minute.

title: Level 19: Epic Boon
text: Gain an Epic Boon or other qualifying feat; Boon of Irresistible Offense suggested.

title: Level 20: Body and Mind
text: Dexterity and Wisdom each rise by 4, capped at 25.

title: Monk Subclass: Warrior of the Open Hand
text: Subclass heading: Warrior of the Open Hand, the Monk's unarmed-combat specialist.

title: Level 3: Open Hand Technique
text: Flurry of Blows hits can Addle (no Opportunity Attacks), Push 15 feet, or Topple prone.

title: Level 6: Wholeness of Body
text: Bonus Action: heal Martial Arts die + Wis mod; uses equal Wis mod per Long Rest.

title: Level 11: Fleet Step
text: After any other Bonus Action, follow up at once with Step of the Wind.

title: Level 17: Quivering Palm
text: Spend 4 Focus on an Unarmed hit to plant vibrations; trigger later for 10d12 Force (Con save halves).

title: Paladin
text: Class heading: the Paladin, a Str/Cha holy warrior with healing, smites and auras.

title: Core Paladin Traits
text: Paladin basics: Str and Cha primary, d10 Hit Die, Wis and Cha saves, all armor and weapons.

title: Becoming a Paladin …
text: Section on how to take the Paladin class, new or multiclassing.

title: As a Level 1 Character
text: Starting as a Paladin: gain all of the core Paladin traits.

title: Paladin Features
text: Table: proficiency bonus, features, Channel Divinity uses, prepared spells and slots by level.

title: As a Multiclass Character
text: Multiclassing into Paladin: Hit Die, Martial weapons, light and medium armor, Shields, level 1 features.

title: Paladin Class Features
text: Intro: Paladin features unlock by class level; see the class table.

title: Level 1: Lay On Hands
text: Healing pool of 5 times your Paladin level HP, refilled on a Long Rest.

title: Level 1: Spellcasting
text: Cast Paladin spells using Charisma; prepare spells and gain slots by level from the class table.

title: Level 1: Weapon Mastery
text: Use mastery properties of two proficient weapon kinds; swap choices after each Long Rest.

title: Level 2: Fighting Style
text: Choose a Fighting Style feat, or Blessed Warrior: two Cleric cantrips cast with Charisma.

title: Level 2: Paladin’s Smite
text: Divine Smite always prepared; cast it once free per Long Rest.

title: Level 3: Channel Divinity
text: Channel divine power, starting with Divine Sense; 2 uses, 1 back per Short Rest, 3 at level 11.

title: Level 3: Paladin Subclass
text: Pick your Paladin specialization at level 3, such as Oath of Devotion.

title: Level 4: Ability Score Improvement
text: Gain an ASI feat (raise ability scores) or another feat you qualify for; repeats at 8, 12, 16.

title: Level 5: Extra Attack
text: Attack action now lets you make two attacks.

title: Level 5: Faithful Steed
text: Find Steed always prepared; cast it once free per Long Rest.

title: Level 6: Aura of Protection
text: You and allies within 10 feet add your Cha mod (min +1) to saving throws.

title: Level 9: Abjure Foes
text: Magic action, 1 Channel Divinity: up to Cha-mod creatures within 60 feet save (Wis) or are Frightened.

title: Level 10: Aura of Courage
text: Allies inside your Protection aura are immune to Frightened.

title: Level 11: Radiant Strikes
text: Melee weapon and Unarmed Strike hits deal an extra 1d8 Radiant.

title: Level 14: Restoring Touch
text: Spend 5 Lay On Hands points per condition to end Blinded, Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Stunned and more.

title: Level 18: Aura Expansion
text: Aura of Protection reach grows to 30 feet.

title: Level 19: Epic Boon
text: Gain an Epic Boon or other qualifying feat; Boon of Truesight suggested.

title: Paladin Spell List
text: Paladin spells listed by level with school; C = Concentration, R = Ritual, M = Material.

title: Paladin Subclass: Oath of Devotion
text: Paladin oath of order and justice: the shining-knight archetype.

title: Level 3: Oath of Devotion Spells
text: Gain always-prepared oath spells at set Paladin levels, per the Devotion spell table.

title: Oath of Devotion Spells
text: Table: Devotion spells at levels 3, 5, 9, 13, 17 (Shield of Faith, Aid, Dispel Magic, etc.).

title: Level 3: Sacred Weapon
text: With Attack action, spend Channel Divinity: melee weapon adds Cha to attacks and can deal Radiant, 10 min.

title: Level 7: Aura of Devotion
text: Allies inside your Protection aura are immune to Charmed.

title: Level 15: Smite of Protection
text: Casting Divine Smite gives you and allies in your aura Half Cover until your next turn.

title: Level 20: Holy Nimbus
text: Bonus Action, 10 min: aura gives sunlight, Radiant damage to enemies, Advantage vs Fiends and Undead; 1/Long Rest.

title: Ranger
text: Class heading: the Ranger, a Dex/Wis wilderness hunter with nature spells.

title: Core Ranger Traits
text: Ranger basics: Dex and Wis primary, d10 Hit Die, Str and Dex saves, 3 skills, light/medium armor.

title: Becoming a Ranger …
text: Section on how to take the Ranger class, new or multiclassing.

title: As a Level 1 Character
text: Starting as a Ranger: take every core trait plus level 1 Ranger features.

title: As a Multiclass Character
text: Multiclassing into Ranger: Hit Die, Martial weapons, one Ranger skill, light/medium armor, Shields.

title: Ranger Class Features
text: Intro: Ranger features unlock by class level; see the class table.

title: Level 1: Spellcasting
text: Cast Ranger spells using Wisdom; prepared spells and slots grow per the class table.

title: Ranger Features
text: Table: proficiency bonus, features, Favored Enemy uses, prepared spells and slots by level.

title: Level 1: Favored Enemy
text: Hunter's Mark always prepared; cast it free twice per Long Rest, more uses later.

title: Level 1: Weapon Mastery
text: Use mastery properties of two proficient weapon kinds; swap choices after each Long Rest.

title: Level 2: Deft Explorer
text: Gain Expertise in one proficient skill and learn two languages.

title: Level 2: Fighting Style
text: Choose a Fighting Style feat, or Druidic Warrior: two Druid cantrips cast with Wisdom.

title: Level 3: Ranger Subclass
text: Pick your Ranger specialization at level 3, such as Hunter.

title: Level 4: Ability Score Improvement
text: Gain an ASI feat (raise ability scores) or another feat you qualify for; repeats at 8, 12, 16.

title: Level 5: Extra Attack
text: Attack action now lets you make two attacks.

title: Level 6: Roving
text: +10 feet Speed out of heavy armor, plus Climb and Swim Speeds equal to Speed.

title: Level 9: Expertise
text: Gain Expertise in two more proficient skills.

title: Level 10: Tireless
text: Magic action: gain 1d8 + Wis temp HP (Wis-mod uses per Long Rest); Short Rests cut Exhaustion.

title: Level 13: Relentless Hunter
text: Damage never forces a Concentration check for Hunter's Mark.

title: Level 14: Nature’s Veil
text: Bonus Action: become Invisible through your next turn; Wis-mod uses per Long Rest.

title: Level 17: Precise Hunter
text: Advantage on attacks against the creature under your Hunter's Mark.

title: Level 18: Feral Senses
text: Gain Blindsight out to 30 feet.

title: Level 19: Epic Boon
text: Gain an Epic Boon or other qualifying feat; Boon of Dimensional Travel suggested.

title: Level 20: Foe Slayer
text: Hunter's Mark damage die becomes d10 instead of d6.

title: Ranger Spell List
text: Ranger spells listed by level with school; C = Concentration, R = Ritual, M = Material.

title: Ranger Subclass: Hunter
text: Ranger subclass that stalks threats to defend nature and people.

title: Level 3: Hunter’s Lore
text: Learn a marked creature's Immunities, Resistances, and Vulnerabilities.

title: Level 3: Hunter’s Prey
text: Choose Colossus Slayer (+1d8 to wounded foes) or Horde Breaker (extra attack nearby); swap on rests.

title: Level 7: Defensive Tactics
text: Choose Escape the Horde or Multiattack Defense; swap after any rest.

title: Level 11: Superior Hunter’s Prey
text: Once per turn, Hunter's Mark extra damage also hits a second creature within 30 feet.

title: Level 15: Superior Hunter’s Defense
text: Reaction on taking damage: resist that type for the rest of the turn.

title: Rogue
text: Class heading: the Rogue, a Dex skill expert with Sneak Attack.

title: Core Rogue Traits
text: Rogue basics: Dex primary, d8 Hit Die, Dex and Int saves, 4 skills, Thieves' Tools, light armor.

title: Becoming a Rogue …
text: Section on how to take the Rogue class, new or multiclassing.

title: As a Level 1 Character
text: Starting as a Rogue: take every core trait plus level 1 Rogue features.

title: As a Multiclass Character
text: Multiclassing into Rogue: Hit Die, one Rogue skill, Thieves' Tools, light armor, level 1 features.

title: Rogue Class Features
text: Intro: Rogue features unlock by class level; see the class table.

title: Level 1: Expertise
text: Expertise in two proficient skills, plus two more at Rogue level 6.

title: Level 1: Sneak Attack
text: Once per turn, add 1d6 (scaling) to a hit with Advantage or an ally near the target.

title: Rogue Features
text: Table: proficiency bonus, features, and Sneak Attack dice (1d6 to 10d6) by level.

title: Level 1: Thieves’ Cant
text: You speak Thieves' Cant plus one extra language of your choice.

title: Level 1: Weapon Mastery
text: Use mastery properties of two proficient weapon kinds; swap choices after each Long Rest.

title: Level 2: Cunning Action
text: Bonus Action each turn: Dash, Disengage, or Hide.

title: Level 3: Rogue Subclass
text: Bonus Action if you haven't moved: Advantage on your next attack, but Speed drops to 0.

title: Level 3: Steady Aim
text: Pick your Rogue specialization at level 3, such as Thief.

title: Level 4: Ability Score Improvement
text: Gain an ASI feat or any feat you qualify for; again at 8, 10, 12, 16.

title: Level 5: Cunning Strike
text: Trade Sneak Attack dice for effects like Poison, Trip, or Withdraw; save DC 8 + Dex + PB.

title: Level 5: Uncanny Dodge
text: Reaction: halve damage from an attack by an attacker you can see.

title: Level 7: Evasion
text: Dex saves for half damage: take none on a success, half on a failure.

title: Level 7: Reliable Talent
text: On ability checks with a proficient skill or tool, treat d20 rolls of 9 or less as 10.

title: Level 11: Improved Cunning Strike
text: Each Sneak Attack can carry two Cunning Strike effects, paying both costs.

title: Level 14: Devious Strikes
text: New Cunning Strikes: Daze (2d6), Knock Out (6d6), and Obscure (3d6, blinds).

title: Level 15: Slippery Mind
text: Become proficient in Wis and Cha saving throws.

title: Level 18: Elusive
text: Attacks against you can't have Advantage unless you're Incapacitated.

title: Level 19: Epic Boon
text: Gain an Epic Boon or other qualifying feat; Night Spirit boon suggested.

title: Level 20: Stroke of Luck
text: Turn a failed D20 Test into a 20; 1 use per Short or Long Rest.

title: Rogue Subclass: Thief
text: Rogue subclass for burglars and explorers: agility, climbing, and magic-item mastery.

title: Level 3: Fast Hands
text: Bonus Action: Sleight of Hand (locks, traps, pockets), Utilize, or use a magic item.

title: Level 3: Second-Story Work
text: Climb Speed equal to Speed; jump distance uses Dex instead of Str.

title: Level 9: Supreme Sneak
text: New Cunning Strike, Stealth Attack (1d6): stay Invisible from Hide if you end in heavy cover.

title: Level 13: Use Magic Device
text: Attune to 4 items, sometimes save charges (d6 roll of 6), and cast from any Spell Scroll.

title: Level 17: Thief’s Reflexes
text: Take two turns in the first combat round: normal Initiative and Initiative minus 10.

title: Sorcerer
text: Class heading: the Sorcerer, a Charisma caster with innate magic and Metamagic.

title: Core Sorcerer Traits
text: Sorcerer basics: Cha primary, d6 Hit Die, Con and Cha saves, 2 skills, simple weapons, no armor.

title: Becoming a Sorcerer …
text: Section on how to take the Sorcerer class, new or multiclassing.

title: As a Level 1 Character
text: Starting as a Sorcerer: take every core trait plus level 1 Sorcerer features.

title: As a Multiclass Character
text: Multiclassing into Sorcerer: gain the Hit Die and level 1 features; see multiclass slot rules.

title: Sorcerer Class Features
text: Intro: Sorcerer features unlock by class level; see the class table.

title: Level 1: Spellcasting
text: Cast Sorcerer spells with Charisma; four cantrips to start, plus prepared spells and slots by level.

title: Sorcerer Features
text: Table: proficiency bonus, features, Sorcery Points, cantrips, prepared spells and slots by level.

title: Level 1: Innate Sorcery
text: Bonus Action, 1 min: +1 Sorcerer spell DC, Advantage on spell attacks; 2 uses per Long Rest.

title: Level 2: Font of Magic
text: Gain Sorcery Points (2 at level 2, rising); convert them to spell slots and back.

title: Creating Spell Slots
text: Table: Sorcery Point cost to make slots, levels 1 to 5 (costs 2, 3, 5, 6, 7).

title: Level 2: Metamagic
text: Learn two Metamagic options and spend Sorcery Points to alter spells; more options later.

title: Level 3: Sorcerer Subclass
text: Pick your Sorcerer specialization at level 3, such as Draconic Sorcery.

title: Level 4: Ability Score Improvement
text: Gain an ASI feat (raise ability scores) or another feat you qualify for; repeats at 8, 12, 16.

title: Level 5: Sorcerous Restoration
text: On a Short Rest, regain Sorcery Points up to half your level; 1 use per Long Rest.

title: Level 7: Sorcery Incarnate
text: Out of Innate Sorcery uses? Pay 2 Sorcery Points; while active, apply 2 Metamagics per spell.

title: Level 19: Epic Boon
text: Gain an Epic Boon or other qualifying feat; Boon of Dimensional Travel suggested.

title: Level 20: Arcane Apotheosis
text: While Innate Sorcery is active, one Metamagic per turn costs no Sorcery Points.

title: Metamagic Options
text: Intro to the alphabetical list of Metamagic options.

title: Careful Spell
text: 1 SP: up to Cha-mod creatures automatically pass the spell's save and take no damage on a success.

title: Distant Spell
text: 1 SP: double a spell's range, or make a Touch spell reach 30 feet.

title: Empowered Spell
text: 1 SP: reroll up to Cha-mod damage dice; stacks with other Metamagic.

title: Extended Spell
text: 1 SP: double a 1-minute-plus spell's duration (max 24 hours); Advantage on Concentration saves.

title: Heightened Spell
text: 2 SP: one target has Disadvantage on its saves against the spell.

title: Quickened Spell
text: 2 SP: cast a 1-action spell as a Bonus Action, if no other level 1+ spell that turn.

title: Seeking Spell
text: 1 SP: reroll a missed spell attack roll; stacks with other Metamagic.

title: Subtle Spell
text: 1 SP: cast with no Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

title: Transmuted Spell
text: 1 SP: change a spell's Fire, Acid, Cold, Lightning, Poison or Thunder damage to another of these.

title: Twinned Spell
text: 1 SP: treat a spell as 1 level higher so it can target one more creature.

title: Sorcerer Spell List
text: Sorcerer spells listed by level with school; C = Concentration, R = Ritual, M = Material.

title: Sorcerer Subclass: Draconic Sorcery
text: Subclass heading: Draconic Sorcery, magic inherited from dragons.

title: Level 3: Draconic Resilience
text: +3 max HP (+1 per later Sorcerer level); unarmored AC = 10 + Dex + Cha.

title: Level 3: Draconic Spells
text: Gain always-prepared dragon spells at set Sorcerer levels, per the Draconic Spells table.

title: Draconic Spells
text: Table: Draconic spells at levels 3, 5, 7, 9 (Chromatic Orb, Fly, Charm Monster, Summon Dragon, etc.).

text: Pick a dragon damage type (Fire, Acid, Cold, Lightning, Poison): resist it, add Cha to one damage roll.

title: Level 14: Dragon Wings
text: Bonus Action: 60-foot Fly Speed for 1 hour; once per Long Rest or 3 Sorcery Points.

title: Level 18: Dragon Companion
text: Cast Summon Dragon free once per Long Rest, no Material component, optionally without Concentration.

title: Warlock

title: As a Level 1 Character
text: Starting as a Warlock: take every core trait plus level 1 Warlock features.

title: As a Multiclass Character
text: Multiclassing into Warlock: Hit Die, light armor, and level 1 features.

text: Intro: Warlock features unlock by class level; see the class table.

text: Gain an ASI feat (raise ability scores) or another feat you qualify for; repeats at 8, 12, 16.
